arxiv-2112-02223.title: A Game-Theoretic Approachfor AI-based Botnet Attack Defence
arxiv-2112-02223.creator: Hooman Alavizadeh, Julian Jang-Jaccard, Tansu Alpcan, Seyit Camtepe
arxiv-2112-02223.description: Abstract The new generation of botnets leverages Artificial Intelligent (AI) techniques to conceal the identity of botmasters and the attack intention to avoid detection. Unfortunately, there has not been an existing assessment tool capable of evaluating the effectiveness of existing defense strategies against this kind of AI-based botnet attack.

arxiv-2306-02598.title: Medial packing, frustration and competing network phases in strongly-segregated block copolymers
arxiv-2306-02598.creator: Michael S. Dimitriyev, Abhiram Reddy, Gregory M. Grason
arxiv-2306-02598.description: Abstract Self-consistent field theory (SCFT) has established that for cubic network phases in diblock copolymer melts, the double-gyroid (DG) is thermodynamically stable relative to the competitor double-diamond (DD) and double-primitive (DP) phases, and exhibits a window of stability intermediate to the classical lamellar and columnar phases.

arxiv-2310-12208.title: Dynamical Friction Models for Black-Hole Binary Formation in AGN Disks Journal: ApJ IAS15 ( Rein & Spiegel 2015 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , NumPy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , Rebound ( Rein & Liu 2012 ) , SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 )
arxiv-2310-12208.creator: Kecheng Qian, Jiaru Li, Dong Lai
arxiv-2310-12208.description: Abstract Stellar-mass black holes (sBH) embedded in gaseous disks of active galactic nuclei (AGN) can be important sources of detectable gravitational radiation for LIGO/Virgo when they form binaries and coalesce due to orbital decay. In this paper, we study the effect of gas dynamical friction (DF) on the formation of BH binaries in AGN disks using N N -body simulations.

arxiv-2406-11023.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning and Partial Transfer Learning for Bearing Fault Diagnosis in the Presence of Highly Missing Data
arxiv-2406-11023.creator: Mohammadreza Kavianpour 1,∗, Parisa Kavianpour 2, Amin Ramezani 1
arxiv-2406-11023.description: Abstract One of the most significant obstacles in bearing fault diagnosis is a lack of labeled data for various fault types. Also, sensor-acquired data frequently lack labels and have a large amount of missing data. This paper tackles these issues by presenting the PTPAI method, which uses physics-informed deep learning- based technique to generate synthetic labeled data.

arxiv-2412-11576.title: DCBM: Data-Efficient Visual Concept Bottleneck Models
arxiv-2412-11576.creator: Katharina Prasse, Patrick Knab, Sascha Marton, Christian Bartelt, Margret Keuper
arxiv-2412-11576.description: Abstract Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) enhance the interpretability of neural networks by basing predictions on human-understandable concepts. However, current CBMs typically rely on concept sets extracted from large language models or extensive image corpora, limiting their effectiveness in data-sparse scenarios. We propose Data-efficient CBMs (DCBMs), which reduce the need for large sample sizes during concept generation while preserving interpretability.

arxiv-2503-17476.title: Birds of a Feather Undermine Equity: A Strategy to Align Intent and Outcome in Team-Based Learning in Higher Education
arxiv-2503-17476.creator: P G Kubendran Amos
arxiv-2503-17476.description: Abstract Efforts to promote equity in higher education often rely on shared intent among instructors and students. Yet, as demonstrated in this study, when students form their own teams for Team-Based Learning (TBL) tasks, they unintentionally cluster with peers of similar socio-economic backgrounds, ultimately undermining equity.

arxiv-2503-21914.title: PyUAT: Open-source Python framework for efficient and scalable cell tracking with uncertainty awareness
arxiv-2503-21914.creator: Johannes Seiffarth, Katharina Nöh
arxiv-2503-21914.description: Abstract Tracking individual cells in live-cell imaging provides fundamental insights, inevitable for studying causes and consequences of phenotypic heterogeneity, responses to changing environmental conditions or stressors. Microbial cell tracking, characterized by stochastic cell movements and frequent cell divisions, remains a challenging task when imaging frame rates must be limited to avoid counterfactual results.

arxiv-2505-02494.title: Roadmap for warm dense matter physics
arxiv-2505-02494.creator: Jan Vorberger, Frank Graziani, David Riley, Andrew D. Baczewski, Isabelle Baraffe, Mandy Bethkenhagen, Simon Blouin, Maximilian P. Böhme, Michael Bonitz, Michael Bussmann, Alexis Casner, Witold Cayzac, Peter Celliers, Gilles Chabrier, Nicolas Chamel, Dave Chapman, Mohan Chen, Jean Clérouin, Gilbert
arxiv-2505-02494.description: Abstract This roadmap presents the state-of-the-art, current challenges and near future developments anticipated in the thriving field of warm dense matter physics. Originating from strongly coupled plasma physics, high pressure physics and high energy density science, the warm dense matter physics community has recently taken a giant leap forward.

arxiv-2507-14851.title: Grounding Degradations in Natural Language for All-In-One Video Restoration
arxiv-2507-14851.creator: Muhammad Kamran Janjua, Amirhosein Ghasemabadi, Kunlin Zhang, Mohammad Salameh, Chao Gao, Di Niu
arxiv-2507-14851.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Muhammad Kamran Janjua, Amirhosein Ghasemabadi, Kunlin Zhang, Mohammad Salameh, Chao Gao, Di Niu. In this work, we propose an all-in-one video restoration framework that grounds degradation-aware semantic context of video frames in natural language via foundation models, offering interpretable and flexible guidance. Unlike prior art, our method assumes no degradation knowledge in train or test time and learns an approximation to the grounded knowledge such that the foundation model can be safely disentangled during inference adding no extra cost.

arxiv-2508-09289.title: Weighted Estimation of the Tail Index under Right Censorship: A
arxiv-2508-09289.creator: Unified Approach Based on Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen Integrals
arxiv-2508-09289.description: Abstract Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen integral estimators to the tail index of right-censored Pareto-type data traditionally rely on the assumption that the proportion p of upper uncensored observations exceeds 1/2, corresponding to weak censoring regime. However, this condition excludes many practical settings characterized by strong censorship, where p\leq 1/2.

arxiv-2510-03820.title: Fixed Point Theorem for Path-Averaged Contractions in Complete b-Metric Spaces MSC2020: 47H10, 54E50 Keywords: Path Averaged Contractions, contractive mapping, fixed point, complete metric space.
arxiv-2510-03820.creator: Nicola Fabiano
arxiv-2510-03820.description: Abstract We extend the fixed point result for Path-Averaged Contractions (PA-contractions) from complete metric spaces to complete b-metric spaces. We prove that every continuous PA-contraction on a complete b-metric space has a unique fixed point, provided the contraction constant α \alpha satisfies s ​ α < 1 s\alpha<1 , where s ≥ 1 s\geq 1 is the b-metric coefficient.

arxiv-2510-18068.title: Cartesian Statistics on Spheres
arxiv-2510-18068.creator: Rudolf Beran
arxiv-2510-18068.description: Abstract Directional data consists of unit vectors in q -dimensions that can be described in polar or Cartesian coordinates. Axial data can be viewed as a pair of directions pointed in opposite directions or as a projection matrix of rank 1.

arxiv-2512-24098.title: Training a Huggingface Model on AWS Sagemaker (Without Tears)
arxiv-2512-24098.creator: Liling Tan
arxiv-2512-24098.description: Abstract Developments of Large language models (LLMs) have been mainly led by resource-rich research groups and industry partners. Without the luxury of on-premise computing resources to train LLMs of growing complexity, researchers are adopting cloud machine learning services like AWS Sagemaker to train Huggingface models.

britannica-1911-agate.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-agate.description: Article 'Agate' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 1), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. In the formation of an ordinary agate, it is probable that waters containing silica in solution—derived, perhaps, from the decomposition of some of the silicates in the lava itself—percolated through the rock, and deposited a siliceous coating on the interior of the vapour-vesicles.

pmc-12673313.title: Evaluation of Carotid Intima-Media Thickness and Other Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Children with Chronic Kidney Disease
pmc-12673313.creator: Nadide Melike Sav, Pelin Kosger, Nuran Çetin, Mehmet Ali Sungur, Birsen Ucar, Selmin Karademir
pmc-12673313.description: ObjectiveThe onset of chronic kidney disease during childhood substantially increases the risk of cardiovascular complications in adulthood among affected patients. In such patients, chronic damage beginning in childhood has been linked to higher long-term mortality rates, and bone changes may also occur due to factors other than renal osteodystrophy.

pmc-12688272.title: Mapping evolutionary paradigm of Oropouche virus driven by dinucleotide bias and context-dependent codon bias
pmc-12688272.creator: Xuanye Yang, Zeyu Liu, Xiaoting Ren, Chunlin Wang, Jianhua Zhou
pmc-12688272.description: Arthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) pose significant public health threats, and understanding their evolutionary mechanisms can inform molecular diagnostics and vaccine design. Oropouche virus (OROV), a relatively understudied arbovirus, exhibits unique evolutionary dynamics in nucleotide composition. We analyzed 45 OROV strains across genotypes to assess selective pressures shaping nucleoprotein, glycoprotein, and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) evolution.

pmc-13352888.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLocal authorities (local government) in England is responsible for promoting a healthy food environment. The food environment includes any opportunity to obtain food which includes physical and virtual environments. However, currently both local and national policy only regulates around restricting types of food available in the physical food environment Over the past decade there has been a substantial rise in the virtual food outlets where customers can only order food online using an app.

pmc-13591546.title: Urine electrolytes guide treatment of Gitelman syndrome and recurrent syncope—A case report
pmc-13591546.creator: Saloni Agrawal, Kenneth M Fifer, Samira S Farouk, Joshua L Rein
pmc-13591546.description: Syncope is a common reason for inpatient admission. Few case studies describe an association between syncope and Gitelman syndrome (GS). Herein, we present a case of a woman with hypokalemia and recurrent syncope which eventually led to a diagnosis of GS. A physiologic approach to urine electrolyte interpretation informed clinical decisions to diagnose and manage complications associated with GS.
